selected_problem: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. Fresh-main inspection found that `WorkspaceService.contextBundle` compared `maxBytes` against filesystem raw byte size before decoding text, but recorded and returned `totalBytes` from the UTF-8 re-encoding of the decoded string. Malformed UTF-8 can expand to replacement characters, so a file whose raw size fits the budget can produce returned context whose actual encoded size exceeds the declared hard budget.

execution.route_basis: The latest canonical main still exposes native complex synthesis as unresolved. The new code reality contains one direct bounded-context integrity defect with a falsifiable malformed-UTF-8 reproduction, so source-contract replay narrows it to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without prescribing a new cognition architecture or forcing mode rotation.

changes: `contextBundle` still rejects symbolic links, non-files and raw files above the per-file size ceiling before reading.
After UTF-8 decoding it now computes `contentBytes=Buffer.byteLength(content)` and applies the total `maxBytes` gate to those actual returned-context bytes before accepting the file.
Accepted-file counting from the previous cycle and all existing credential/path/type admission boundaries remain intact.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against fresh main: a 100-byte file containing 0xff decoded to replacement characters whose re-encoded context size was 300 bytes. With maxBytes=150 the old bundle accepted it and returned totalBytes > 150, so the hard context budget was false.

truth_boundaries: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. This makes the declared context-byte ceiling truthful for decoded strings; it does not guarantee semantic sufficiency or optimal context selection.
Context files are still decoded as UTF-8 with replacement semantics; this cycle only ensures replacement expansion cannot violate the returned byte budget.
Initial semantic seed priority across many otherwise admissible files remains a separate selection-quality question.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
